source.title: Localizing Memorization in SSL Vision Encoders
source.authors: Wen-Hao Wang; Adam Dziedzic; Michael Backes; Franziska Boenisch

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures localization and unit-level memorization in self-supervised vision encoders and reports how training augmentations and weight decay change memorization. It also compares SSL with supervised learning, but does not measure the generalization gap claimed by the versions.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own reported measurements of memorization and the downstream-accuracy effects of pruning or replacing components identified by those measurements. This study does not test arbitrary-label fitting, test error versus training error, optimizer or batch-size effects on that gap, dropout, sharpness, or removal of memorized examples followed by retraining. Cited findings from prior work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study measures memorization localization in SSL encoders and the effects of pruning units or replacing layers on downstream accuracy. None of V1–V8 is tested. In particular, pruning memorizing units is different from V8's removal of memorized training examples followed by retraining. References to memorization supporting generalization supply motivation, not a test of that version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that their metrics localize SSL memorization across layers and units: deeper layers generally have higher accumulated memorization, highly memorizing units occur throughout encoders, atypical examples show greater memorization, and ViT memorization concentrates more in fully connected sublayers. SSL emphasizes individual-example memorization whereas supervised models increasingly emphasize classes. Their interventions suggest potential applications to selective fine-tuning and pruning. Augmentation and weight-decay effects are additional findings, not tests of V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses self-supervised representation learning and measures internal memorization localization, rather than supervised natural-label generalization or the training-test error gap in the listed source methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Training augmentation strength and weight decay change measured memorization; measurement augmentation choice changes UnitMem; LayerMem measurement distance metric and candidate subset size/composition have little reported effect. Training framework comparisons show similar patterns for matched architectures and datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: LayerMem generally increases with depth, while highly memorizing units occur throughout the encoder; ViT fully connected sublayers show more memorization than attention sublayers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SSL vision encoders distribute instance memorization across layers and units, with architecture-dependent localization.

fits_no_version.finding: SSL units show greater individual-example than class memorization, while supervised models increasingly show class memorization in deeper layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SSL and supervised training produce different patterns of instance and class selectivity.

fits_no_version.finding: Stronger augmentation, weight decay and differential privacy reduce measured memorization; stronger weight decay also reduces linear-probing accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training choices affect memorization localization in SSL encoders and can carry downstream performance costs.

fits_no_version.finding: Pruning high-UnitMem units causes greater downstream accuracy loss than random or low-UnitMem pruning; replacing highly memorizing layers also causes greater accuracy changes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorization localization identifies encoder components whose removal or replacement strongly affects downstream performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning layers chosen by ΔLayerMem yields higher reported STL10 accuracy than fine-tuning equally many last layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorization-informed layer selection can improve selective fine-tuning in the tested SSL setup.

fits_no_version.finding: CIFAR100-pretrained SSL representations have higher mean probing accuracy on the other tested datasets than supervised representations, with the reverse ordering on CIFAR100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training objectives affect the transfer performance of ResNet9 representations.

record.code_released: not stated as a URL; supplementary code is said to be attached, and code is said to be uploaded to OpenReview
record.problems: The measures quantify internal memorization rather than the train-test error gap; many plotted results have no exact values in the text; some appendix tables are flattened or have apparent transcription issues; only the explicitly described small set of experiments is captured here. Several reported outcomes are downstream linear-probing accuracy, not generalization-gap measurements.
record.rows_left_out: Not every per-layer score in Appendix G Tables 29–33 or every repeated pruning/replacement condition is individually expanded; the core positive, negative, and condition-changing outcomes are retained. Table 6’s flattened later rows prevent reliable mapping of all 20% and total-pruning values. Appendix C.7 Table 24(b) is not mapped because values are absent in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Fixed-random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy and chance performance on random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifier test error and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets and recovery recipes.
Training batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epochs and adapted recipes.
Dropout's effects on held-out error, dataset-size dependence and joint dropout/weight-decay removal.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps and competing measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus random examples and retraining; dataset dependence.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not negate the reported localization effects. Held-out accuracy is relevant to several versions without requiring a train–test gap, but these experiments lack the specific comparisons those versions name. No omitted result in the supplied text tests a listed version, so missing is empty.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or natural-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep or test-error measurement around interpolation.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison of held-out performance.
No batch-size comparison of held-out performance under epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap comparison.
No removal of highly memorized training examples followed by retraining.
